origin.description: Extract several code-point ranges from every string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector, or another vector that can be coerced to character.

arguments.name: start, end
arguments.text: Inclusive positions. A flat pair of vectors is shared by every string. A list of vectors gives each string its own starts. A two-column matrix is one set of ranges applied to every string.

origin.details: This function does not use the strict vctrs size check. A flat start and end are one shared set of ranges, so each string contributes several pieces. Names on string are copied onto the outer list.
origin.value: A list the same length as string. Each element is a character vector.
origin.example:
x <- c("abcde", "ghifgh")
parts <- str_sub_all(x, c(1, 2), c(2, 4))
cat(paste0("str_sub_all(x, c(1, 2), c(2, 4)) returns ", paste(vapply(parts, function(item) paste(item, collapse = " "), ""), collapse = " | "), ".\n"))

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those.

arguments.name: start
arguments.text: A flat index vector, a list of index vectors, an IndexMatrix, a two-column dict, or a locate matrix with colnames.

arguments.name: end
arguments.text: The inclusive end for a flat start or a list of starts. Not used when start is a matrix.

translation.details: A plain list of rows is a list of per-string starts, matching a list in R. An IndexMatrix, a dict, or a matrix that carries colnames is one shared set of ranges. Names on string are copied to the outer list.
translation.value: A list of lists of strings, one inner list per string.
translation.example:
from stringr.sub import str_sub_all
pair = str_sub_all(["abcde", "ghifgh"], [1, 2], [2, 4])
print("str_sub_all(x, c(1, 2), c(2, 4)) returns " + " | ".join(" ".join(item) for item in pair) + ".")
